summary: The candidate captures much of the paper's central surgery, Kirby-calculus, ribbon-Hopf, modular-category, purification, and RT-invariant pipeline, with generally sound formulas and mostly plausible page locators. However, it is an unnormalized raw pool with duplicate IDs, several classification errors, incomplete external attribution, convention ambiguity in the dual-module entry, and important missing or only partially represented entries.
strengths: Correctly extracts the main Lickorish–Wallace, Kirby-calculus, ribbon-category, modular-category, purification, and Reshetikhin–Turaev results.
Most displayed Hopf-algebra, R-matrix, quantum-trace, Kirby-color, and normalization formulas are mathematically close to the gold conventions.
Page-level locators are present for nearly all entries, and the candidate includes useful supporting constructions such as colored ribbon graphs, evaluation/coevaluation, and pivotal structure.
issues: Important gold entries are missing or not independently represented: the Hopf-algebra definition, Kirby reduction proposition, twist definition, ribbon graphical calculus, colored framed-link invariance proposition, finite simple system/domination, Hopf-link matrix, modular data, and the universal-twist lemma.

Several entries have the wrong class/type: coproduct action, R-matrix braiding, and colored-link evaluation are labeled as definitions rather than lemmas/propositions; quantum-trace results are labeled as calculations rather than the corresponding claim/lemma.

The raw pool contains six duplicate IDs, including duplicated duality, ribbon-category, quasitriangular, ribbon-Hopf, categorical-dimension, and Turaev-functor entries, reducing distinct coverage and creating redundancy.

The extra Rohlin cobordism theorem is not part of the gold entry set and its stated attribution/strengthened handlebody conclusion is insufficiently grounded; some Turaev and other external results also lack explicit source attribution.
The dual-module entry offers an S^{-1}-based alternative despite the gold's fixed S-based duality convention, and the framing entry omits the integer framing-coordinate statement.
The signature-normalization formula uses D and Delta without a separately extracted modular-data definition, while the negligible-module entry omits the gold's explicit negligible-morphism condition.
